extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs), GME program directors, accrediting organizations, and policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed Medicare IPPS/LTCH PPS regulatory provisions covering low-volume hospital payment adjustments, MDH program changes, GME/IME payment methodology, nondiscrimination requirements, and criteria for determining when a residency program is 'new' for cap-building purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-volume hospital mileage criterion (FY 2027 Oct–Dec 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the portion of FY 2027 beginning October 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026, a hospital must be located more than 15 road miles from the nearest subsection (d) hospital, as reflected in proposed revised § 412.101(b)(2). (Road miles defined in § 412.101(a) to mean “miles” as defined in § 412.92(c)(1).)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For establishing that the hospital meets the mileage criterion, the use of a web-based mapping tool as part of the documentation is acceptable. The MAC will determine if the information submitted (name and street address of nearest hospital(s), location on a map, and distance) is sufficient; if not, the MAC will follow up to obtain additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-volume hospital mileage criterion (FY 2027 Jan–Sep 2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: To meet the mileage criterion to qualify for the low-volume hospital payment adjustment for the portion of FY 2027 beginning January 1, 2027 through September 30, 2027, a hospital must be located more than 25 road miles from the nearest subsection (d) hospital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Road miles defined as in § 412.101(a). Use of a web-based mapping tool is acceptable for documentation; MAC determines sufficiency and may follow up for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-volume hospital discharge criterion (Oct 1–Dec 31, 2026 period)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the portion of FY 2027 beginning October 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026, the hospital must have less than 3,800 discharges total, including both Medicare and non-Medicare discharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written verification must state, based upon the most recently submitted cost report, that the hospital meets this discharge criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-volume hospital discharge criterion (Jan 1–Sep 30, 2027 period / statutory revert)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the portion of FY 2027 beginning on January 1, 2027 (when discharge criteria revert to pre-FY2011 statutory requirements), the hospital must have less than 200 discharges total, including both Medicare and non-Medicare discharges (as described in examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written verification must state, based upon the most recently submitted cost report, that the hospital meets this discharge criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and submission deadlines for low-volume hospital status requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital must make a written request for low-volume hospital status that is received by its MAC by September 1 immediately preceding the start of the Federal fiscal year for which applying; for the January 1, 2027 portion a written request must be received by December 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hospital's request is received after the deadline and the MAC determines the hospital meets criteria, the MAC will apply the applicable low-volume payment adjustment prospectively within 30 days of the MAC's low-volume status determination. A hospital may submit a single request covering both portions of FY 2027 by the September 1, 2026 deadline or submit separate requests by the respective deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required in written request/verification for low-volume status
rubrics_metrics.description: The written request/verification to the MAC must include sufficient documentation to establish that the hospital meets the applicable mileage and discharge criteria, including name and street address of nearest hospital(s), location on a map, distance from the hospital requesting status, and a statement (based on most recent cost report) that the hospital meets the discharge criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: state that the hospital is located more than 15 road miles (Oct–Dec) or more than 25 road miles (Jan–Sep), and state the total discharge count (e.g., less than 3,800 or less than 200, as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: MAC determination and evidentiary sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) will determine if the information submitted by the hospital (addresses, map location, and distance) is sufficient to document that it meets the mileage criterion; if not sufficient, the MAC will follow up to obtain additional necessary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of web-based mapping tools as part of documentation is explicitly acceptable; MAC discretion applies in evaluating submitted evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation without reapplying for hospitals that qualified in prior year
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital that qualified for the low-volume hospital payment adjustment for FY 2026 may continue to receive a low-volume hospital payment adjustment for FY 2027 without reapplying if it meets both the discharge criterion and the mileage criterion applicable for FY 2027 (for both portions of the year as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a hospital must send written verification that is received by its MAC no later than the applicable deadlines (September 1, 2026 and/or December 1, 2026) stating it meets the mileage and discharge criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDH program conforming regulatory changes for extension through Dec 31, 2026
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes conforming changes to regulations governing the Medicare-dependent, small rural hospital (MDH) program at § 412.108(a)(1) and (c)(2)(iii) and the general payment rules at § 412.90(j) to reflect the legislative extension of the MDH program through December 31, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the MDH program is extended beyond December 31, 2026 by statute, CMS would modify proposed conforming changes depending on timing relative to the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration effect of MDH program
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the MDH program extension in Public Law 119-75 covers only through December 31, 2026, beginning January 1, 2027 the MDH program will no longer be in effect and, absent further Congressional action, hospitals that previously qualified for MDH status will be paid based on the Federal rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes prior policy allowing MDHs to apply for SCH status in advance of MDH expiration and related reapplication rules if program were extended again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option for MDHs to apply for Sole Community Hospital (SCH) status
rubrics_metrics.description: When the MDH program was set to expire in prior years, CMS revised SCH policies to allow MDHs to apply for SCH status in advance of expiration and be paid as such under certain conditions; these policies are codified at § 412.92(b)(2)(i) and (v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provider that classifies as SCH in anticipation of MDH expiration would have to reapply for MDH classification per 42 CFR 412.108(b) and meet classification criteria at 42 CFR 412.108(a) if the MDH program is later extended and the provider wishes to return to MDH classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: GME direct payment (PRA) methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct GME payments are based on a hospital-specific base-period per resident amount (PRA) calculated by dividing a hospital's allowable direct costs of GME in a base period by its number of full-time equivalent (FTE) residents in the base period; the base-period PRA is updated annually for inflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For most hospitals, the base period is the cost reporting period beginning in FY 1984 (Oct 1, 1983–Sep 30, 1984). Direct GME payments are the updated PRA multiplied by weighted FTE residents and the hospital's Medicare share of total inpatient days. See 42 CFR 413.75 through 413.83 for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IME adjustment methodology and FTE cap limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The IME adjustment is applied to DRG payments based on the ratio of the hospital's number of FTE residents (training in inpatient/outpatient departments and eligible non-provider sites) to the number of inpatient hospital beds. Congress established limits (caps) on the number of allopathic and osteopathic residents that a hospital could include in its FTE resident count based on the hospital's unweighted FTE count in its most recent cost reporting period ending on or before December 31, 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps apply for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 1997; dental and podiatric residents are excluded from the statutory cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'approved medical residency training program' and accreditation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An "approved medical residency training program" is a residency or other postgraduate medical training program participation in which may be counted toward certification in a specialty or subspecialty and includes formal postgraduate training programs in geriatric medicine approved by the Secretary; in general, an 'approved' program is accredited by one of several national accrediting bodies or leads toward board certification by the ABMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program approval and related terms are defined in regulations at §§ 412.105(f)(1)(i), 413.75(b), and 415.152.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory accreditation criteria for GME accrediting bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Accrediting organizations may not use accreditation criteria that promote or encourage discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or religion, including use of those characteristics or intentional proxies as a selection criterion for employment, program participation, resource allocation, or similar activities or benefits; prohibited practices include conduct violating federal antidiscrimination laws and any 'unlawful practices' under the Attorney General's Guidance for Recipients of Federal Funding Regarding Unlawful Discrimination (July 29, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy finalized in the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule applied to accrediting bodies; the proposed rule extends a similar policy to approved medical residency programs themselves (effective Oct 1, 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination requirement proposed for approved medical residency programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement that, in addition to meeting other applicable requirements, an approved medical residency training program must not discriminate, or promote or encourage discrimination, on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or religion, including use of those characteristics or intentional proxies as a selection criterion for employment, program participation, resource allocation, or similar activities or benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to consolidate existing and proposed non-discrimination requirements under a new 42 CFR 413.84 and cross-reference it in §§ 412.105(f)(1)(i), 413.75(b), and 415.152; effective date proposed as Oct 1, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing 'new program' criteria (program newness primary test)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered a 'new' medical residency program for cap-building purposes, existing regulation (as adopted Aug 27, 2009) requires the program to satisfy three primary criteria: the program director is new; and the teaching staff are new; and the residents are new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy was adopted to prevent transfer/duplication of existing programs' cap slots; CMS has historically allowed that 'overwhelming majority' of residents and staff not coming from previous programs preserves newness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed resident 'newness' threshold (FY 2025 proposal) — 90% rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In the FY 2025 proposed rule, CMS proposed that, in order for a residency program to be considered new, at least 90 percent of the individual resident trainees (not FTEs) must not have previous training in the same specialty as the new program; if more than 10 percent transferred from another program in the same specialty, the program would be ineligible for new cap slots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS solicited comment on exceptions for small/rural programs and on defining 'small' (suggested as accredited for 16 or fewer positions); CMS also sought feedback on thresholds for faculty newness and commingling and on handling of transfers/replacements due to Match results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced review policy proposals based on resident newness percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback suggested an 'enhanced review' framework: 100% new residents = program qualifies as new without further review; at least 90% but less than 100% new residents = program must demonstrate residents have not previously trained in an existing residency program in the same specialty with any faculty or with the program director from the new residency program; less than 90% new residents = program does not qualify as new (subject to exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recommended allowances for replacements, limiting application to Program Year 1 residents, or excluding Match-driven exceptions; CMS considered these comments in proposing modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and safe harbors for small or rural programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged CMS to create exceptions to new program requirements for small and/or rural programs; a majority suggested defining a 'small' program as accredited for 16 or fewer resident positions (some recommended different ceilings or that only programs in underserved areas qualify).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed/considered lenient criteria included higher thresholds, full exemption for qualifying small programs, or alternate thresholds; CMS solicited input on what should be considered 'small' and what exceptions are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations regarding hiring experienced faculty/program directors
rubrics_metrics.description: While earlier guidance considered faculty and program director newness, commenters overwhelmingly opposed restrictions on hiring experienced faculty and program directors. CMS proposes that, effective for programs started on or after October 1, 2026, it would no longer consider the previous employment of the faculty or program director in determining whether a residency program should be considered genuinely new for cap-building purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS concluded that considering the previous training experience of residents is a sufficient guardrail to prevent inappropriate transfers of cap slots, and thus removal of faculty/program director employment restrictions is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential procedural accommodations for resident replacements and Match outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters recommended that programs be allowed to replace departing residents with other residents at the same training level without counting against compliance with the newness threshold, that the 90 percent requirement apply only to Program Year 1 entrants, and that programs be allowed to demonstrate they would have met thresholds but for Match outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other suggestions included interim reviews during cap-building periods, excluding previously trained residents from final cap calculations, or limiting only the number of residents admitted from the same existing program. CMS requested public comment on these operational issues.
